chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about a man who was praying when the Imam left, and the man had already prayed one rak'ah of the obligatory prayer. He (AS) said: 'If the Imam is just (adl), he should pray another (rak'ah), then conclude (salat) and make it voluntary (tafaddul), and enter with the Imam in his prayer. If the Imam is not just, he should build upon his prayer as it is, and pray one more rak'ah with him, and sit for the duration of saying: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' Then he should complete his prayer with him as much as he can, for precaution (tawqiyyah) is broad, and there is nothing of precaution except that its owner is rewarded for it, if Allah wills.'
And it is also possible that he meant by his saying 'and make it obligatory' as a discharge (qada') for what was missed of the obligatory duties. That is indicated by what he narrated:

key_terms.إِمَاماً عَدْلاً: A just Imam (one who is legally qualified and pious)
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةَ: Precaution (often used in Shia fiqh to denote flexibility in ritual acts to avoid error or harm)

ai.seo_question: What should a worshipper do if the Imam leaves during congregational prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith details the fiqh of congregational prayer when the Imam departs prematurely, distinguishing between a just (adl) Imam, where the worshipper may complete the prayer as voluntary, and a non-just one, where they build upon the existing prayer. It highlights the Shia principle of *tawqiyyah* (precaution), asserting that the worshipper is rewarded for adapting their prayer structure to maintain congregational unity or validity despite the Imam's absence. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the continuity of prayer behind varying levels of Imamate authority.
